spans.s:
दुश् दुश्, euphonically substituted for दुस्
in comp. like दुश्-चक्षस्. See bottom of col. 3.

दुष् 1. दुष्, euphonically substituted for
दुस् in दुष्-कर &c. See p. 425, col. 1.

दुष् 2. दुष्, cl. 4. P. (ep. also A.) दुष्-
यति, -ते, दुदोष, दोक्ष्यति, अदुषत्
(according to Vopa-deva also अदुक्षत्), दोष्टुम्,
to become bad or corrupted, to be ruined, to perish,
suffer damage, to be soiled; to be or become
depraved or defiled or impure, to be violated (as a
woman), to be contaminated by a crime, to sin, to
commit a mistake, to be wrong; to be faithless or
unchaste (as a wife): Caus. दूषयति (ep. also
-ते), -यितुम्, to corrupt, spoil, make bad, cause to
perish, hurt, destroy, lay waste, to make unclean or
impure, to soil, defile, contaminate, vitiate, taint; to
dishonour or violate (as a girl or the wife of another);
to cause evil or misfortune (in astrology); to corrupt
the morals, deprave, demoralize; to adulterate; to
falsify; to rescind, abrogate, annul, retract; to object,
refute, disprove; to find fault with, speak ill of,
accuse, blame, abuse, contemn; (it is to be observed
that दूष्यते, Pass. of the Caus., may often more cor-
rectly be read where दुष्यते is given in the printed
editions of epic poems, the sense of दूष्यते being
the same; according to Pāṇ.

, another form
of the Caus., viz. दोषयति, &c., is optionally used in
speaking of moral corruption, e. g. कामो दूषयति
or दोषयति चित्तम्, lust corrupts the mind.)

दुस् दुस्, ind. (related to rt. 2. दुष्, and
reckoned by Pāṇini among the Upa-sargas), a particle
and prefix to nouns and rarely to verbs, implying
evil, bad, badly, wicked, wickedly, difficult, hard, with
difficulty, slight, inferior, &c., and sometimes equiva-
lent to the English prefix इन्- or उन्-; [cf. rt. 2. दुष्;
rt. 1. द्विष्: Zend dush, dus-mananh, dush-i-ti:
Gr. δυς e. g. δυσ-μενής: Goth. tus in tuz-veryan:
Old Germ. zur-: Hib. do, do-dhail, ‘bad luck;’
do-dhuine, ‘a bad man;’ do-dheanta, ‘hard to be
done;’ do-bhasuighte, ‘immortal.’] दुस् becomes
दुर्, q. v., before vowels and soft consonants; becomes
दू, q. v., before र्; remains unchanged before त्, थ्
(not however in the earlier language where स् becomes
ष् and the following त्, थ् are changed to ट्, ठ्);
becomes दुष् and rarely दुः before क्, ख् [cf. दुः-
ख], प्, फ्; becomes दुः and rarely दुस्, दुश्, दुष्
before स्, श्, and ष्. Those compounds in which दुस्
becomes दुर् and दू will be found under दुर् and
दू respectively. The other compounds formed with
दुस् are as follow.
—दुः-पच, दुः-पतन, दुः-
पत्त्र, दुः-प्रज्ञ, &c., see दुष्-पच, &c., p. 425,
col. 2.
—दुः-शंस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. wishing evil,
malevolent, malicious, wicked.
—दुः-शक or दुः-
शक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुः-शक्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, having no
power, possessed of little power, powerless.
—दुः-
शल, अस्, m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-
rāṣṭra; (आ), f., N. of the only daughter of Dhṛta-
rāṣṭra, (she was the wife of king Jayad-ratha.)
—दुः-शस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, badly recited; (अम्), n.
a bad recitation.
—दुः-शाक, अम्, ind. the luckless
Śākas (see Pāṇ.

).
—दुः-शास, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be controlled.
—दुः-शासन, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be governed, intractable, difficult to be
managed; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of
Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—दुः-शासु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. wishing
evil, malevolent.
—दुः-शीम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. =
दुष्-प्राप, difficult to be attained; (अस्), m., N.
of a man?; [cf. सु-शीम.]
—दुः-शील, अस्, आ, अम्,
badly disposed, ill-behaved, reprobate, abandoned.
—दुःशील-ता, f. bad behaviour, badness of disposi-
tion.
—दुः-शृङ्गी, f. a disloyal wife.
—दुः-शेव,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘badly propitious,’ envious; (Sāy.)
difficult to serve (as if सेव); delighting in evil.
—दुः-शोध, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be cleaned.
—दुः-शोष, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be dried.
—दुः-श्रुत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly or wrongly heard.
—दुः-षन्त, अस्, m., N. of the father of
Bharata; [cf. दौःषन्ति; later forms are दुष्-
मन्त, दुष्यन्त, दुष्वन्त, दुःष्वन्त.]
—दुः-षम, अस्, आ, अम्, unlike, uneven; adverse,
unlucky, unfortunate; wrong; (अम्), ind. unevenly,
improperly; at a wrong time; (आ), f. (with Jainas)
N. of two spokes in the wheel of time, viz. the fifth
[]
in the Ava-sarpiṇī, and the second in the Ut-sarpiṇī;
[cf. दुः-सम.]
—दुःषम-सुषमा, f. ‘both
unfortunate and fortunate’ (but with a preponderance
of misfortune), N. of two spokes in the Jaina wheel
of time, viz. the fourth in the Ava-sarpiṇī, and the
third in the Ut-sarpiṇī.
—दुः-षह, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. difficult to be borne, irresistible; [cf. दुः-सह.]
—दुः-षुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sleeping badly, having
bad dreams.
—दुः-ष्टुत and दुः-ष्टुति, see दु-
ष्टुत, दु-ष्टुति, p. 425, col. 2.
—दुः-ष्वप्न्य,
अम्, n., Ved. ‘causing bad dreams,’ evil dream, pain;
(Sāy.) poverty; [cf. जाग्र-द्˚, स्वप्न-द्˚, दौः-
ष्वप्न्य, दुः-स्वप्न.]
—दुः-संलक्ष्य, अस्,
आ, अम्, difficult to be observed or recognised.
—दुः-
संस्कार, अस्, m. a bad custom or practice.
—दुः-
सक्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुः-सक्थि, इस्, इस्, इ, having
deformed thighs.
—दुः-सङ्ग, अस्, m. bad inclina-
tion, evil attachment.
—दुः-सञ्चार, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be passed.
—दुः-सञ्चिन्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be conceived or imagined.
—दुः-सत्त्व,
अम्, n. an evil being, noxious creature, ferocious
animal.
—दुःसत्त्व-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, filled with or
infested by evil beings or ferocious animals.
—दुः-
सन्तुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, unsatisfied, discontented.
—दुः-सन्धान or दुः-सन्धेय, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be joined together or united or reconciled.
—दुः-सम, अस्, आ, अम्, unequal, uneven, unlucky,
unfit, improper, evil, bad, unseasonable; [cf. दुः-
षम.]
—दुः-समतिक्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult
to be surmounted, insurmountable.
—दुः-समी-
क्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be observed or per-
ceived.
—दुः-सम्पाद or दुः-सम्पाद्य, अस्, आ,
अम्, difficult to be reached or attained.
—दुः-
सह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be borne, unbearable,
irresistible; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of
Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; of a son of Puru-kutsa and father
of Sam-bhūti; of an evil demon; (आ), f. an epithet
of Śrī; N. of a shrub (= नाग-दमनी); [cf. दुः-
षह, दुर्-विषह, दुष्-प्रसह.]
—दुः-स-
हाय, अस्, आ, अम्, having evil companions or asso-
ciates.
—दुः-साक्षिन्, ई, m. a false witness.
—दुः-
साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be accomplished;
difficult to be managed; difficult to be cured; diffi-
cult to be conquered.
—दुः-सेव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, diffi-
cult to be used or dealt with, hard to be managed,
intractable.
—दुः-स्त्री, f. a bad woman.
—दुः-
स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘standing badly,’ badly fixed,
unsteady, disquieted; badly circumstanced, suffering
pain or affliction, distressed, unhappy; unwell, ill,
badly situated, ill-conditioned, poor, miserable; igno-
rant, unwise, a fool; (अम्), ind. badly, ill, unwell;
in bad circumstances.
—दुः-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, =
दुः-स्थ above; (अम्), n. an improper manner
of standing.
—दुः-स्थिति, इस्, f. instability, unsteadi-
ness; ill condition, bad fortune, unhappiness.
—दुः-
स्थेय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be stood; (अम्), n.
difficult standing or position.
—दुः-स्नान, अम्, n.
defective or inauspicious ablution.
—दुः-स्पर्श, अस्,
आ, अम्, difficult or unfit to be touched or laid hold
of, unpleasant to the touch; (अस्), m. the prickly
plant Alhagi Maurorum (= लता-करञ्ज); (आ), f.,
N. of several plants, Solanum Jacquini [cf. क्षुद्र-
द्˚]; Alhagi Maurorum, Mucuna Pruritus, Cassyta
Filiformis.
—दुः-स्पृश, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
touched; [cf. दुः-स्पर्श.]
—दुः-स्पृष्ट or दु-
स्पृष्ट, अम्, n. slight contact, the slight action of
the tongue which produces the sounds य्, र्, ल्, व्;
(अस्), m. a sound produced by this slight motion of
the tongue.
—दुः-स्फोट, अस्, m. ‘difficult to be
burst,’ a sort of weapon.
—दुः-स्वन, अस्, आ, अम्,
sounding badly, cacophonous.
—दुः-स्वप्न, अस्, m. a
bad dream.
—दुःस्वप्न-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, seeing
a bad dream.
—दुःस्वप्न-नाश, अस्, m. the removal
of bad dreams.
—दुःस्वप्न-नाशन, अस्, आ, अम्,
removing bad dreams.
—दुःस्वप्न-प्रतिबोधन,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be awakened from sleep.
—दुःस्वप्नोपशान्ति (˚न-उप्˚), इस्, f. the cessa-
tion of a bad dream.
—दुश्-चक्षस्, आस्, आस्, अस्,
Ved. evil-eyed.
—दुश्-चर्, cl. 1. P. -चरति,
-रितुम्, to act wrongly or badly towards (with
acc. of person), to behave badly.
—दुश्-चर, अस्,
[]
आ, अम्, difficult to be gone to or approached,
unattainable, inaccessible, difficult to be passed or
spent (as time); difficult to be performed or accom-
plished; going with trouble or difficulty; acting ill,
behaving wickedly; (अस्), m. a bear (as moving
slowly); a bivalve shell.
—दुश्चर-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ,
practising very difficult penance.
—दुश्चर-त्व, अम्,
n. inaccessibility, difficulty of being approached or
practised.
—दुश्-चरित, अस्, आ, अम्, misbehaving,
wicked, abandoned; (अम्), n. misbehaviour, misdoing,
ill-conduct, wickedness; (आनि), n. pl. (with Buddhists)
the ten chief sins, viz. murder, theft, adultery, lying,
calumny, lewdness, evil speech, covetousness, envy,
heresy.
—दुश्चरितिन्, ई, इनी, इ, performing wicked
actions.
—दुश्-चर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, affected with
disease of the skin, leprous; a circumcised man,
one whose prepuce is naturally or artificially wanting;
[cf. दौश्चर्म्य.]
—दुश्-चारित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, or
दुश्-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, badly conducted, misbehaving.
—दुश्-चिकित्स, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be cured,
incurable.
—दुश्-चिकित्सा, f. (in medic.) wrong
treatment.
—दुश्-चिकित्सित or दुश्-चिकित्स्य, अस्, आ,
अम्, difficult to be cured.
—दुश्चिकित्स्य-तम, अस्,
आ, अम्, most difficult to be cured.
—दुश्चिकित्स्य-
त्व, अम्, n. difficulty of being cured, incurableness.
—दुश्-चित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. thinking evil.
—दुश्-चिन्त्य,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be thought about or under-
stood.
—दुश्-चेष्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, misbehaving,
doing or designing evil; (अम्), n. evil purpose or
action, misconduct, error.
—दुश्-च्यवन or दुश्-
च्याव or दुश्-च्यावन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
felled or brought to the ground, unshaken, unmov-
able; (अस्), m. an epithet of Indra; (another etymo-
logy for the latter meaning is based upon the legend,
that Indra having raised his arm to hurl his thunder-
bolt at Cyavana, had it fixed in that position by the
curse of the saint.)
—दुश्-छद, अस्, आ, अम्,
‘covering badly,’ forming a bad garment; difficult
to be clothed, hardly covered, tattered.
—दुश्-छिद्,
त्, त्, त्, difficult to be cut or destroyed.
—दुश्-
छिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, badly cut or separated, badly
extracted.
—दुष्-कर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, difficult
or hard to be done or performed or accomplished;
difficult to be reached or attained; difficult, arduous
(with inf., e. g. दुष्करं कर्तुम्, difficult
to perform); difficult to be borne or supported;
doing badly or with difficulty, acting badly, wicked,
bad; (अम्), n. difficult or painful act, a difficult
task, a difficulty; atmosphere, ether; the tree of
plenty?; (अम्), ind. hardly, scarcely (with following
यदि).
—दुष्करकारि-ता, f. the state of experi-
encing difficulties.
—दुष्कर-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ex-
periencing difficulties, suffering what is hard to
be borne.
—दुष्कर-चर्या, f. ‘the performance
of difficulties,’ N. of the seventeenth chapter of the
Lalita-vistara which describes Śākya-muni as the
performer of difficult tasks.
—दुष्-करण, अम्, n.
anything difficult to be done or performed, a diffi-
cult task.
—दुष्-कर्ण, अस्, m., N. of one of the
100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (also read दुः-कर्ण.)
—दुष्-कर्मन्, अ, n. evil act, crime, wickedness,
sin; any difficult or painful act; (आ, आ, अ), acting
wickedly, wicked, criminal.
—दुष्-कलेवर, अस्,
अम्, m. n. ‘the bad or miserable body,’ i. e. the
body considered as the seat of diseases &c.
—दुष्-
कायस्थ-कुल, अम्, n. the miserable writer-caste.
—दुष्-काल, अस्, m. ‘bad or all-destroying time,’
an epithet of Śiva.
—दुष्-कीर्त्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, dis-
honourable.
—दुष्-कुल, अम्, n. a low family or
race; (अस्, आ, अम्), of a low family, low-born; [cf.
दौष्कुल, दौष्कुलेय, दौष्कुल्य.]
—दुष्-
कुल-ता, f. lowness of origin, meanness of birth or
family.
—दुष्कुलीन, अस्, आ, अम्, of a low or
degraded family or race, low-born; (अस्), m. a sort of
perfume, commonly called Chora.
—दुष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्,
Ved. an evil-doer, offender, wicked, criminal.
—दुष्-
कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done wrongly or wickedly, done
with difficulty or pain, badly organized, badly applied
(e. g. दुष्कृता पूजा, badly applied worship);
(अम्), n. evil action, misdeed, sin, crime, guilt.
—दुष्कृत-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, acting wickedly,
[]
wicked, reprobate, a criminal; (अ), n. a wicked deed,
wickedness.
—दुष्कृत-वहिष्कृत, अस्, आ, अम्,
free from sin.
—दुष्कृतात्मन् (˚त-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ,
evil-minded, wicked, base.
—दुष्-कृति, इस्, इस्, इ,
or दुष्कृतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, acting wickedly, an evil-
doer.
—दुष्-कृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. badly
ploughed, ill-cultivated.
—दुष्-क्रम, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult of access; going ill; ill-arranged, unme-
thodical.
—दुष्-क्रिया, f. evil act, a misdemeanour.
—दुष्-क्रीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly purchased, bought
too dearly.
—दुष्-ख, see दुःख at p. 418,
col. 2.
—दुष्-खदिर, अस्, m. a tree related to
the Acacia Catechu (= खदिर).
—दुष्-टनु, उस्,
वी, उ, Ved. having an ugly body, having an odious
form.
—दुष्-टर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. difficult to be
crossed or passed, hard to be overcome, unconquer-
able, invincible, irresistible; not to be subdued; not
to be surpassed or excelled; difficult to be endured;
[cf. the later form दुस्-तर.]
—दुष्-टरीतु, उस्,
उस्, उ, Ved. = दुष्-टर; (उस्), m. epithet of Indra;
N. of a man.
—दु-ष्टुत, अम्, n. (for दुः-ष्टुत),
Ved. faulty recitation of the Stotra.
—दु-ष्टुति, इस्,
f. (for दुः-ष्टुति), Ved. a faulty or bad hymn.
—दुष्ठु, उस्, उस्, उ (for दुः-स्थु), ‘standing
badly,’ ill-behaved, depraved; (उ), ind. ill, bad;
improperly, incorrectly; [cf. दौष्ठव and सु-
ष्ठु.]
—दुष्-पच, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
digested.
—दुष्-पतन, अम्, n. falling badly,
(formed to explain अप-भ्रंश.)
—दुष्-पत्त्र,
अस्, m. a kind of perfume, commonly called Chora;
(also read दुः-पत्त्र.)
—दुष्-पद, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. (according to Sāy. = दुष्-प्रपदन), not
to be reached or overtaken.
—दुष्-पराजय, अस्,
आ, अम्, difficult to be conquered; (अस्), m., N.
of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—दुष्-
परिग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be seized or kept.
—दुष्-परिणाम, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
finished or ended.
—दुष्-परिहन्तु, उस्, उस्, उ,
Ved. difficult to be destroyed or disturbed.
—दुष्-
परीक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be investigated or
examined.
—दुष्पर्श, see दुः-स्पर्श.
—दुष्-
पान, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be drunk.
—दुष्-
पार, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be crossed or passed
over; difficult to be accomplished or performed.
—दुष्-पार्ष्णिग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, having a dan-
gerous enemy in the rear; (also read दुः-पार्ष्णि-
ग्राह.)
—दुष्-पीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly drunk.
—दुष्-पुत्र, अस्, m. a bad son.
—दुष्-पुरुष,
अस्, m. a bad man; (also read दुः-पुरुष; cf.
दौष्पुरुष्य.)
—दुष्-पूर, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult
to be filled or satiated or satisfied.
—दुष्-प्रकम्प
or दुष्-प्रकम्प्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
shaken or agitated, immovable.
—दुष्-प्रकाश,
अस्, आ, अम्, ‘lighting badly,’ obscure, dark.
—दुष्-
प्रकृति, इस्, इस्, इ, evil-natured, bad-tempered.
—दुष्-प्रजस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (प्रजस् = प्रजा), hav-
ing bad offspring.
—दुष्-प्रज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्,
having a weak intellect, weak-minded, stupid; [cf.
दुःप्रज्ञ.]
—दुष्प्रज्ञ-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity.
—दुष्-प्रज्ञान, अम्, n. want of understanding,
weak intellect; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. weak in intellect,
stupid.
—दुष्-प्रणीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly led, badly
conducted or trained, ill-managed; (अम्), n. im-
prudent or impolitic conduct; ill luck, evil fortune;
[cf. दुर्-नीत.]
—दुष्-प्रतर, अस्, आ, अम्, diffi-
cult to be passed over or crossed.
—दुष्-प्रतिग्रह,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be taken or laid hold of.
—दुष्-प्रतिवारण, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
warded off or averted.
—दुष्-प्रतिवीक्षणीय or
दुष्-प्रतिवीक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be looked
at, one whose glance is unbearable.
—दुष्-प्र-
धर्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, not to be assailed or meddled
with; difficult to be attacked; secure from assaults,
intangible, not to be touched; (अस्), m., N. of one
of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (आ), f., N. of
two prickly plants which cannot be touched, =
खर्जूरी, Phœnix Sylvestris; = दुर्-आलभा, Alhagi
Maurorum; [cf. दुर्-आधर्ष and दुर्-धर्ष.]
—दुष्-प्रधर्षण, अस्, ई, अम्, = दुष्-प्र-
धर्ष; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of
Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (ई), f., N. of the plant Melongena
[]
Incurva; [cf. वार्ताकी.]
—दुष्-प्रधर्षिणी, f.
(wrong form for दुष्-प्रधर्षणी, according to
some) = कण्टकारी, = बृहती.
—दुष्-प्रधृ-
ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुष्-प्रधर्ष.
—दुष्-प्र-
पदन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be overtaken or
attained.
—दुष्-प्रमय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to
be measured, immeasurable.
—दुष्-प्रलम्भ,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be deceived; (according to
others) difficult of attainment.
—दुष्-प्रवाद, अस्,
m. calumnious report, slander, defamation.
—दुष्-
प्रवृत्ति, इस्, f. bad news, sad intelligence.
—दुष्-
प्रवेश, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be entered; (आ), f.
a kind of tree, = कन्थारी.
—दुष्-प्रसह, अस्,
आ, अम्, difficult to be borne or supported or suffered,
hard to endure or resist, irresistible; terrible, frightful;
(अस्), m., N. of a Jaina teacher; [cf. दुष्-प्रसा-
ह, दुर्-विषह, दुः-सह, दुः-षह.]
—दुष्-
प्रसाद or दुष्-प्रसादन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult
to be propitiated or conciliated or appeased.
—दुष्-
प्रसाधन (perhaps wrongly read for दुष्-प्र-
सादन) or दुष्-प्रसाध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult
to be managed or dealt with (as a bad-tempered
man).
—दुष्-प्रसाह, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुष्-प्र-
सह.
—दुष्-प्रहर्ष, अस्, m. ‘bad rejoicing,’
N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—दुष्-
प्राप or दुष्-प्रापण or दुष्-प्राप्य, अस्, आ,
अम्, difficult of attainment, hard to attain, difficult
to be reached, unattainable, remote.
—दुष्-प्रावी,
ईस्, ईस्, इ, Ved. difficult of access, unfavourable, un-
friendly.
—दुष्-प्रीति, इस्, f. displeasure.
—दुष्-
प्रेक्ष or दुष्-प्रेक्षणीय or दुष्-प्रेक्ष्य,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be looked at, disagreeable to
the sight.
—दुष्मन्त, अस्, m. another form for
दुष्यन्त below; [cf. दौष्मन्त, दौष्मन्ति,
सुष्मन्त.]
—दुष्यन्त, अस्, m. (a later form
for दुः-षन्त, q. v.), N. of a prince of the lunar
line or descendant of Puru, husband of Śakuntalā
and father of Bharata; [cf. दौष्यन्त and दौष्-
यन्ति.]
—दुष्वन्त, अस्, m. another form for
दुष्यन्त, q. v.; [cf. दौष्वन्ति and दुः-ष्वन्त.]
—दुष्वप्न्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = दुः-ष्वप्न्य,
q. v.
—दुस्-तप, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be endured
(as a penance).
—दुस्-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुस्-
तरण, अस्, ई, अम्, or दुस्-तरणीय, or दुस्-तार,
अस्, आ, अम्, or दुस्-तीर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be
crossed or passed over, hard to be traversed, impassa-
ble, hard to be subdued, invincible; [cf. the older
form दुष्-टर.]
—दुस्-तर्क, अस्, m. false reason-
ing, bad reasoning, wrong argument.
—दुस्तर्क-
मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, founded on false or wrong reason-
ing.
—दुस्-तर्क्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be sup-
posed or reasoned about.
—दुस्-तोष, अस्, आ, अम्,
difficult to be satisfied.
—दुस्-त्यज or दुस्-त्याज्य,
अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be relinquished or quitted.
—दुस्थ, दुस्थित, दुस्पृष्ट, see दुः-स्थ,
दुः-स्पृष्ट.

दुश्चिक्य दुश्चिक्य, अम्, n. (in astrology) N.
of the third lunar mansion.

दुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, become bad, spoiled, cor-
rupted, reduced to a bad state, injured, damaged,
ruined, spoiled, vitiated, contaminated, diseased,
tainted, infected, degraded; depraved; violated;
corrupt, vicious, wicked; bad, evil; faulty, guilty,
convicted, culpable; having evil intentions, ill-affected;
roguish, low, vile; worthless; painful; (आ), f. a bad
woman, a harlot, an unchaste woman; (अम्), n. sin,
an offence, crime, guilt; a kind of Costus, Costus
Speciosus, = कुष्ठ.
—दुष्ट-गज, अस्, m. a
vicious elephant.
—दुष्ट-चरित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, ill-
conducted.
—दुष्ट-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, practising evil
deeds, wicked, criminal.
—दुष्ट-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्,
[]
evil-minded, malevolent, bad-hearted.
—दुष्ट-ता,
f. or दुष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. badness, wickedness; per-
versity, falsehood; contamination, defilement, viola-
tion.
—दुष्ट-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or दुष्ट-बुद्धि,
इस्, इस्, इ, having bad thoughts, evil-minded, evil-
affected.
—दुष्ट-भाव, अस्, आ, अम्, evil-natured, of
a wicked or depraved nature, innately bad or wicked.
—दुष्टभाव-ता, f. wickedness, innate depravity.
—दुष्ट-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, evil-minded, wicked,
depraved.
—दुष्ट-मानस, अस्, ई, अम्, evil-minded,
depraved in mind.
—दुष्ट-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, speaking
evil, uttering bad language.
—दुष्ट-वृष, अस्,
m. a bad or vicious ox, a strong but stubborn ox
which refuses to draw.
—दुष्ट-व्रण, अस्, m. a
dull boil or sore, an obstinate tumor; a sinus.
—दुष्टात्मन् (˚ट-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, of a bad nature,
evil-minded, wicked.
—दुष्टान्वित (˚ट-अन्˚), अस्,
आ, अम्, defiled, rendered impure.
दुष्ट दुष्ट. See col. 1.
दुष्टि, इस्, f. corruption, corruptness, depravity.

दुष्टीय, Nom. P. दुष्टीयति, &c., to become
bad or corrupted (?).
दुष्ठु दुष्ठु. See p. 425, col. 2.
दुष्यन्त दुष्यन्त. See p. 425, col. 3.

दुस्सथ दुस्सथ, अस्, m. a cock; a dog;
(perhaps for दुः-सक्थ.)
दुस्सनि दुस्सनि, इस्, m., N. of a man.
दूश्य दूश्य, अम्, n. = दूष्य, a tent.

दूष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, corruptible, liable to be
corrupted or defiled or contaminated; liable to be
ruined, to be seduced or dishonoured, deserving
censure, condemnable; reprehensible, culpable, con-
temptible, vile, bad; (अस्), m. a wicked man; (अम्),
n. matter, pus, poison; (अम्), n. clothes or a kind
of cloth; cotton, calico; a tent (in this sense perhaps
for दूश्य; cf. दूर्श); (आ), f. an elephant's leathern
girth; [cf. चूषा and कक्ष्या.]
—दूष्य-युक्त,
अस्, आ, अम्, associated with a vile rascal.

दूष दूष, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus. of rt.
2. दुष्), defiling, polluting, contaminating, corrupt-
ing, (generally at the end of comp.; cf. कोर-द्˚ and
पङ्क्ति-द्˚.)

दूस दूस, अम्, n. (considered as an affix),
milk, (occurring in अवि-दूस, q. v.)

दूषक, अस्, इका, अम्, making bad, corrupting,
polluting, contaminating, vitiating, spoiling, violating,
dishonouring, disgracing, seducing, making mischief,
hurting [cf. चर्म-दूषिका]; committing an offence
against, offending, trespassing; disfiguring; acting
against a command or precept; an offender, a seducer,
corrupter, any infamous or wicked person; sinful,
wicked (as an action); वेदानां दूषकस्, one
who vitiates or is a disparager of the Vedas; (इका),
f. a pencil or paint-brush; impurity or secretion of
the eyes, rheum of the eyes [cf. दूषीका]; a kind
of rice.

दूषण, अस्, ई, अम्, corrupting, spoiling, ruining,
destroying, vitiating, contaminating, dishonouring,
violating; offending against; counteracting [cf. अरा-
ति-द्˚, कृत्या-द्˚, खर-द्˚, विष-द्˚]; (अस्), m., N.
[]
of a Rakṣas or Rākṣasa who was one of the
generals of Rāvaṇa; of a Daitya slain by Śiva; (आ),
f., N. of a deity, the wife of Bhauvana and mother of
Tvaṣṭṛ; (अम्), n. the act of spoiling or corrupting,
ruining, vitiating, contaminating, hurting; violating
(a contract), breaking (an agreement), dishonouring
or violating a woman; slighting, speaking ill of any
one, abusing, finding fault, censuring, disparaging,
blaming, detracting, throwing doubts upon, criticising,
objecting, refuting, rendering suspected; objection,
adverse argument; fault, defect, offence, guilt, sin,
blame; [cf. अर्थ-द्˚ and दोष.]
—दूषणारि
(˚ण-अरि), इस्, m. ‘the enemy of Dūṣaṇa,’ epithet
of Rāma.
—दूषणावह (˚ण-आव्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
occasioning guilt.

दूषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, corruptible, liable to be
vitiated, &c., = दूष्य.

दूषयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, making bad, corrupting,
defiling, &c.
दूषयाण, अस्, आ, अम्, vitiating, defiling, spoiling.

दूषयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or दूषयित्नु, उस्, उस्,
उ, a corrupter, one who dishonours or deflowers or
violates (a girl).

दूषि, इस्, इस्, इ, (at the end of comp.) corrupting,
ruining, destroying [cf. अराति-द्˚, आत्म-द्˚, कृत्या-
द्˚]; (इस्), f., Ved. a poisonous substance; (इस्, ई),
f. = दूषिका, दूषीका, the rheum of the eyes.
—दूषी-विष, अम्, n. a vegetable poison that
ceases to act because it has become old or decomposed
(दूषित).
—दूषीविषारि (˚ष-अरि), इस्, m. a
kind of antidote.
—दूष्य्-उदर, अम्, n. a disease
of the abdomen caused by poisonous substances.
—दूष्युदरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, affected with the above
disease.

दूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, corrupted, spoiled, conta-
minated; violated, hurt, injured; demoralized;
disgraced; blamed, censured; calumniated, falsely
accused, often at the end of comp., see मन्यु-द्˚,
शत्रूपजाप-द्˚; (आ), f. a girl who has been violated
or deflowered.

दूषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, corrupting, contaminating,
violating.

दूषीका, f. the secretion or rheum of the eyes;
[cf. दूषिका under दूषक, दूषि.]

दूष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, offending, insulting (for
दूषयत् ?).
